scope: The lone whole-token idućih form in the four Latin sources, at base line 23208, following the separately closed eight-token iduč-family audit.
choice: Normalize idućih to idučih, preserving its genitive plural participial inflection and all surrounding syntax.
motivation: Official grammar explicitly derives and exemplifies the idti present active participle as iduči. Its soft-adjective genitive plural is idučih. The lone ć is a Serbo-Croatian surface intrusion; the seven other inflected iduči controls in this edition all use č.
alternatives_rejected: Retaining idućih was rejected because it conflicts with the verb-specific official example Iduči and with every other iduči-family form in the edition.
Recasting to a lexical adjective such as poprědnyh was rejected because the meaning is genuinely going back to Gauss, not merely previous.

A blanket ć-to-č participle rewrite was rejected because other lexical families, including prior dictionary-controlled slědujući forms, have separate recorded authority and are outside this idti-specific decision.

evidence.official_grammar: Official verbs.md, 21426 bytes, SHA-256 3684BE0634F0163DDD4BEC09719280C3C0E1E2367009AA3DAE584C50DD6249AD: lines 168-176 derive first-conjugation present active participles in -uči, explicitly exemplify Iduči, and prescribe soft-adjective inflection; lines 225-229 establish idti.
evidence.edition_controls: Before this edit the four-source edition contains seven other inflected iduči forms, all with č: iduče three, idučego two, iduči one, idučemu one. EDIT-0111 inventories and protects them. No exact idučih existed only because this is the sole genitive-plural slot.
